readback_body:
## Description

A follow-up static review at `main@8990fc28ffc6099656e5fbd0e4b25ad20e9c3e14` found a **verified ControlModeSession forwarder liveness hazard**, independent of the tmux Client's ingress budget (#2380) and adapter output-byte budget (#2387).

`ControlModeSession::forward_events` is the **single ordered** event consumer from `TmuxClient::EventStream`. For every `TmuxEvent::Resize`, it awaits `note_and_forward(&resize_tx, &observed, cols, rows)`. That helper awaits `resize_tx.send((cols, rows))` on an `mpsc` channel of capacity 16 **without a deadline or closed/full-channel disposition**. If the resize receiver stays alive but stops draining, the 17th distinct resize can leave this single forwarder suspended; later pane Output and SourceLost cannot be processed by that forwarder.

This is not #1352 (backend lock held across a resize handler's await), #2283 (browser parser/resize ordering), or #2286 (authorized active-device viewport ownership). It is an independent queue-consumer liveness failure on the Agent's tmux session adapter.

**Evidence status:** code-path and feasible backpressure ordering verified from source; no real-tmux outage or deterministic red-before test was run in this review. This Issue requires reproduction before an end-to-end production incident is asserted.

### Prototype

- Decision: Not needed
- Reason / interaction uncertainty: backend queue lifecycle; existing terminal UI/degraded state unchanged.
- Status: Not needed

## Reproduction

1. Build a test using the real `ControlModeSession::forward_events` and `note_and_forward` functions, fed by a real `TmuxClient::EventStream` duplex fixture.
2. Give the resize receiver capacity 16 and hold it open **without receiving**; keep output receiver actively draining.
3. Feed 17+ *distinct, otherwise valid* `TmuxEvent::Resize` notifications through the ordered Client source, then a numbered `TmuxEvent::Output` payload and optionally a simulated source loss.
4. Observe whether the output and source-loss handoff complete within an explicit deadline. The current unbounded `resize_tx.send(...).await` can suspend the entire forwarder.
5. Repeat with real isolated tmux `-C` (opt-in `-CC` where supported), a stalled resize subscriber and a healthy output consumer. Verify the actual source stream and recovery state; do not assume an artificial resize flood is a common user workload.

Source:
- [resize channel capacity](https://github.com/BestNathan/nession/blob/8990fc28ffc6099656e5fbd0e4b25ad20e9c3e14/crates/nession-agent/src/tmux/control.rs#L54-L67)
- [single ordered forwarder](https://github.com/BestNathan/nession/blob/8990fc28ffc6099656e5fbd0e4b25ad20e9c3e14/crates/nession-agent/src/tmux/control.rs#L503-L531)
- [unbounded resize send](https://github.com/BestNathan/nession/blob/8990fc28ffc6099656e5fbd0e4b25ad20e9c3e14/crates/nession-agent/src/tmux/control.rs#L534-L548)

## Root Cause

The ordered event forwarder awaits a count-bounded **but time-unbounded** resize queue send. Its only failure path is receiver-drop; a receiver that is alive but stalled never triggers that error, so later output and source-loss events cannot advance. The `observed` size guard is updated **before** the blocking send, creating additional risk of treating an unforwarded size as already propagated.

## Impact

Potential indefinite terminal output freeze during resize bursts and slow downstream consumers; delayed source-loss propagation and inaccurate understanding of resize delivery. A confirmed live incident has not been established.

## Fix Direction

- Define an end-to-end bounded admission/degradation policy for resize notifications without silently dropping authoritative state transitions. Do **not** fix by an unsequenced `try_send` drop or split Output/Resize into independent unordered owners.
- If coalescing is considered, prove it retains final authoritative pane size, never invents a stream cursor, and is compatible with the Agent event/output ordering contract. Otherwise fail closed with explicit source loss and recovery.
- Preserve source ordering and terminal-session epoch/generation fencing on P2P and Relay, including restart/reattach and ControlLease changes.
- Test blocked resize consumer, consumer drop, full queue, output-after-resize, resize-after-output, cancellation/source loss and healthy peer isolation.

## Location

- `crates/nession-agent/src/tmux/control.rs` — `OUTPUT_CHANNEL_CAPACITY`, `RESIZE_CHANNEL_CAPACITY`, `forward_events`, `note_and_forward`
- `crates/nession-agent/src/server/websocket.rs` — Agent output and resize forwarder consumers
- Existing Control Mode/terminal consistency tests

### Success Criteria

- [x] SC-01 With a deliberately stalled, live resize consumer and more than 16 distinct authoritative resizes, terminal output/source-loss handling makes bounded, explicit progress or fails closed within a specified deadline (never silently freezes).
- [ ] SC-02 For real isolated tmux, output and resize remain semantically ordered at the Agent epoch/seq boundary under stalled and recovering subscribers; P2P/Relay observe no silent gap, stale geometry or false continuity.
- [x] SC-03 Existing capture/live checkpoint cut, Resize dedup, active ControlLease and healthy subscriber progress remain intact across queue-full, consumer-drop and reconnect negative fixtures.

## Acceptance Plan

```yaml
acceptance:
  SC-01:
    when: pr
    method: agent
  SC-02:
    when: merged
    branch: staging
    method: case
  SC-03:
    when: pr
    method: agent
```

**Integration-runner prerequisite:** SC-02 requires isolated staging credentials, authenticated revision/Run/Attempt and executable Case provenance; until then it stays Pending, not N/A or inferred Pass.

## Product alignment

- [x] VISION.md: reliable continuous terminal control across devices.
- [x] PRINCIPLE.md: internal failure transparency without permanent UI changes.
- [x] Reviewed `crates/nession-agent/AGENTS.md`, `docs/design/terminal/ahp-inspired-terminal-consistency.md` and `docs/architecture/agent-tmux-control-transport.md`.
- [x] No duplicate source of truth; ControlModeSession remains the session adapter.

**Deduplication:** #1352 protects a different backend mutex lifetime; #2286 owns active-device size authority; #2387 addresses adapter **output-byte resource budget**, not resize-queue liveness; #2380 owns typed Client ingress, not this adapter channel.
